How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, April 16, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Chan
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of April 2, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of April 2, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 24-14 ADDING THE POSITION OF ASSISTANT TO THE
  CITY MANAGER TO THE AUTHORIZED POSITION CLASSIFICATION AND
  SALARY SCHEDULE AND RECLASSIFYING THE POSITION OF
  MANAGEMENT ANALYST-PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER TO ASSISTANT
  TO THE CITY MANAGER IN ADMINISTRATION

  In January 2024, the Management Analyst-Public Information Officer (PIO) position
  within Administration was vacated. Since that time, staff has assessed the operational
  needs to the department and determined that the Management Analyst-PIO position
  should be reclassified to Assistant to the City Manager to cover a greater range of
  administrative duties and functions. If approved by Council, a classification
  specification and salary range for Assistant to the City Manager will be added to the
  City’s Authorized Position Classification and Salary Schedule, and the Management
  Analyst-PIO position in Administration will be reclassified to Assistant to the City
  Manager. The annualized cost impact for reclassifying the Management Analyst-PIO
  position to Assistant to the City Manager in Administration is $37,076.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-14, which
  approves the classification specification and base salary range for Assistant to
  the City Manager, adds the Assistant to the City Manager position classification
  and base salary range to the Authorized Position Classification and Salary
  Schedule, and reclassifies the Management Analyst-PIO to Assistant to the City
  Manager in Administration.

  D. AUTHORIZE ACCEPTANCE OF SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT
  PROGRAM (STEP) GRANT IN THE AMOUNT OF $140,000 [RESOLUTION
  NO. 24-17]

  The Police Department has received a renewed grant from the Office of Traffic
  Safety (OTS) to participate in the Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)
  for Federal Fiscal Year 2023-2024. The grant will reimburse the City for overtime
  costs incurred while participating in this campaign, and for the purchase of
  related equipment for training up to $140,000.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-17 approving
  and accepting the requirements of the Office of Traffic Safety Grant Agreement
  outlined in the report.

  E. POLICE DEPARTMENT PURCHASE OF THREE FRONTLINE VEHICLES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $181,859.46 AND ONE UNMARKED DETECTIVE BUREAU
  VEHICLE IN THE AMOUNT OF $59,168.08 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-19]

  Three 2017-2018 Ford Explorer Interceptors frontline patrol vehicles are past
  their useful life as they all have over 100,000 miles and are exhibiting significant
  mechanical issues. An unmarked police unit is also requested for use in the
  Detective Bureau. The frontline police units have been budgeted for
  replacement in Fiscal Year 2023-2024. The unmarked police unit has been
  budgeted for replacement in Fiscal Year 2023-2024 utilizing Air Quality
  Management District (AQMD) funding. This police unit qualifies as a “Clean Air
  Vehicle” since Staff opted to purchase the hybrid variant of the 2025 Ford
  Explorer Interceptor.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Police Chief to purchase
  the vehicles as listed in the quotations for an amount not to exceed $241,027.54
  and to adopt Resolution No. 24-19, increasing appropriations in the Special
  Projects Fund (Fleet Maintenance) by $984.93 and Air Quality Management
  District by $9,168.08.

  F. THEATRE FEE REDUCTION REQUEST BY SAN GABRIEL MISSION HIGH
  SCHOOL

  San Gabriel Mission High School has requested a partial waiver of theatre rental
  fees for their upcoming graduation ceremony, scheduled for Thursday, May 30,
  2024. The request is for a $3,043 fee reduction, to reduce their total rental cost
  to $5,000. The current rental subsidy account has sufficient funds to cover
  $1,100 in rental fee reduction.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  4
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve staff’s recommendation to
  grant a partial waiver of the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse rental fee in the
  amount of $1,100 for the May 30th event day.

  G. COLLECTION AGREEMENT WITH PROFESSIONAL CREDIT TO PERFORM
  ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE COLLECTION SERVICES FOR DELINQUENT
  CUSTOMER ACCOUNTS

  From time to time, the City needs collection services to help collect money
  owed to the City. Previously, the City had an agreement with Account Recovery
  Services to provide collection services for delinquent receivable accounts.
  Account Recovery Services underwent a change in ownership, and all active
  collection accounts were transferred to FCR Collection Services, operating
  under the name FedChex. With the unexpected change, staff took the
  opportunity to perform an assessment of the collection service providers to
  determine if the City was receiving the best overall value available. The
  proposed agreement with Professional Credit includes an 18% collection fee.
  This fee would only apply to the delinquent accounts that the City requested
  collection services for and is contingent upon the collection of a portion or the
  entire outstanding amount. The City is not charged a fee when funds are not
  collected.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a Professional Services Agreement with Professional Credit to perform
  accounts receivable collection services for delinquent customer accounts.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 706 AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW FOR ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (ZTA24-
  001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  5
   The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 897 (“SB 897”) and Assembly Bill
  2221 (“AB 2221”) in 2022, amending existing State law pertaining to Accessory
  Dwelling Units (ADU) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADU). The new bills
  took effect on January 1, 2023. An ADU ordinance that is not in full compliance
  with the amended State Law became invalid at the time the laws took effect.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines, the
  amendment to a Zoning Ordinance is not considered a project as defined in
  Section 15378 and can be seen with certainty that it will not have a significant
  effect on the environment. The proposed amendment to the Zoning Ordinance
  qualifies for this CEQA exemption as there is no possibility that the ordinance will
  have a significant effect on the environment as it amends the City’s Municipal
  Code to demonstrate compliance with State ADU Law.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss the proposed Ordinance No. 706.

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 706 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING
  UNITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS.

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting. The
  Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after the adoption.

  Alternative Option for Consideration:

  Provide comments and direct staff to return at a later date with revisions to the
  amendment for the City Council’s review and approval.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  6
   A. CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 707 DELETING TITLE
  III, CHAPTER 33, SECTIONS 33.50-3.57 FROM THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO DISSOLVE THE HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND
  RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION AND POTENTIAL APPOINTMENT OF
  TWO COUNCILMEMBERS TO A HUMAN RELATIONS SUBCOMMITTEE

  The Human Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR) Commission was established
  by the City Council on October 20, 2020 through Ordinance No. 670. Since then,
  the HEAR Commission has hosted monthly meetings to accomplish the goals
  set forth in their annual workplans to advance the purpose and mission of the
  Commission. At the March 5, 2024 City Council meeting, Council requested that
  the dissolution of the HEAR Commission be placed on the agenda of a future
  meeting for consideration. Adopting Ordinance No. 707 would result in the
  dissolution of the Commission. Also under consideration is the creation of a
  new subcommittee comprised of two Council Members to provide guidance to
  the full City Council on any future human relations issues in San Gabriel. There
  is no fiscal impact associated with discussing the dissolution of the HEAR
  Commission. Should the City Council adopt the attached ordinance, there will
  be a small budget savings for the expenses that were approved to support the
  HEAR Commission, as well as a reduction in the staff time involved in
  supporting a commission.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council determine the preferred course of
  action pertaining to the future of the HEAR Commission. Possible actions are
  as follows and are not mutually-exclusive; for example, the City Council could
  choose to do items one and two below.

  1. Waive full reading, introduce by title only, and waive future reading of
  Ordinance No. 707 Deleting Title III, Chapter 33, Sections 33.50-3.57 from
  the San Gabriel Municipal Code to dissolve the HEAR Commission; and
  waive future reading and schedule the second reading and adoption of the
  Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.

  2. Appoint two members of the City Council to an ad hoc subcommittee and
  provide specific direction on a human relations issue to explore and provide
  recommendations to the entire City Council.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 16, 2024  7
   3. Appoint two members of the City Council to a standing Brown Act
  subcommittee to explore human relations issues in San Gabriel. Issues
  could be assigned at any time in the future to the subcommittee as needed.

  4. Provide new direction to the HEAR Commission that aligns with the needs
  of the City as well as the purpose and scope of the HEAR Commission,
  including but not limited to amendments to the 2024 annual workplan,
  purpose, and scope of the Commission.

  5. Do nothing, thereby maintaining full operation of the HEAR Commission in
  its existing capacity.

  6. Other options that the City Council determines appropriate after discussing
  the item.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, May 7, 2024 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF APRIL 16, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:34 P.M.
  on Tuesday, April 16, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Chan

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,
  Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Assistant City Clerk Marilyn
  Bonus, and Management Assistant Adam Yang.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Assistant City Clerk Bonus provided information for the public on how to view the meeting
  and request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Wu announced that the agenda order was approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS - None.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

I  Benjamin Tran requested a resolution be agendized to call for a ceasefire in the Gaza
  Strip.

  Elias requested a resolution be agendized to call for a ceasefire in Palestine.

  Peter Deng, resident, speaking on behalf of the medical center on the second floor at
  123 E. Valley Blvd., requested that zoning be changed to allow the medical center to
  be on the first floor to be more accessible to seniors.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 6  April 16, 2024
   Valerie Munoz, La Puente Council member and San Gabriel's representative to the San
  Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority, invited the Council and community to tour the
  Authority and provided information about its activities.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Assistant City Clerk · Bonus stated staff's request that Item 4A2 be approved as
  amended with the removal of a partial sentence and correction of a typographical
  error.

I  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Counci l Member .
  Harrington, to approve Consent Calendar Item 4A as amended and Items 4B - 4G as
  presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of April 2, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of April 2, 2024.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

I  The City Council approved March 21, and March 29, 2024, Registers of Demands
  and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 24-14 ADDING THE POSITION OF ASSISTANT TO THE CITY
  MANAGER TO THE AUTHORIZED POSITION CLASSIFICATION AND SALARY
  SCHEDULE AND RECLASSIFYING THE POSITION OF MANAGEMENT
  ANALYST-PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER TO ASSISTANT TO THE CITY
  MANAGER IN ADMINISTRATION

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-14, which approves the classification
  specification and base salary range for Assistant to the City Manager, adds the
  Assistant to the City Manager position classification and base salary range to the
  Authorized Position Classification and Salary Schedule, and reclassifies the
  Management Analyst-PIO to Assistant to the City Manager in Administration.

  D. AUTHORIZE ACCEPTANCE OF SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM
  (STEP) GRANT IN THE AMOUNT OF $140,000 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-17]

I  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-17 approving and accepting the
  requirements of the Office of Traffic Safety Grant Agreement outlined in the report.

  E. POLICE DEPARTMENT PURCHASE OF THREE FRONTLINE VEHICLES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $181,859.46 AND ONE UNMARKED DETECTIVE BUREAU
  VEHICLE IN THE AMOUNT OF $59,168.08 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-19]

  The City Council authorized the Police Chief to purchase the vehicles as listed in
  the quotations for an amount not to exceed $241,027.54 and adopted Resolution

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  April 16, 2024
   No. 24-19, increasing appropriations in the Special Projects Fund (Fleet
  Maintenance) by $984.93 and Air Quality Management District by $9,168.08.

  F. THEATRE FEE REDUCTION REQUEST BY SAN GABRIEL MISSION HIGH
  SCHOOL

  The City Council approved staff's recommendation to grant a partial waiver of the
  San Gabriel Mission Playhouse rental fee in the amount of $1,100 for the May 30 th
  event day.

I  G. COLLECTION AGREEMENT WITH PROFESSIONAL CREDIT TO PERFORM
  ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE COLLECTION SERVICES FOR DELINQUENT
  CUSTOMER ACCOUNTS

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to enter into a Professional Services
  Agreement with Professional Credit to perform accounts receivable collection
  services for delinquent customer accounts.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 706 AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW FOR ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (ZTA24-001)
  - INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  Mayor Wu opened the public hearing.

  Associate Planner Marlon Cervantes made the staff presentation.

I  Clarifying discussion included that this item is to bring the City's Code into
  compliance with State Code.

  There was no public comment; therefore, Mayor Wu closed the public hearing.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Chan,
  to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 706 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS AND JUNIOR

I

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  April 16, 2024
   A. CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 707 DELETING TITLE 111,
  CHAPTER 33, SECTIONS 33.50-33.57 FROM THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO DISSOLVE THE HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR)
  COMMISSION AND POTENTIAL APPOINTMENT OF TWO COUNCILMEMBERS
  TO A HUMAN RELATIONS SUBCOMMITTEE

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation.

  The following provided comments or spoke in favor of continuing the HEAR

I
  Commission: Fr. John Molyneux, CMF, resident; Rick Khan; Jorge Montes, resident;
  Amanda Andradre, resident; Stacia Kato, President, PFLAG San Gabriel Valley Asian
  Pacific Islander Chapter; Cristian Castaneda, resident; Natalia Castaneda, resident;
  Lori Chu, resident; Kevin Chu, resident; Anonymous, resident; Jose Escobar,
  Regional Health Officer, San Gabriel Valley, County of Los Angeles Public Health;
  James E. Herr, Director, Daniel K. Inouye National Center for the Preservation of
  Democracy; Yolie Anguiano; Jason Moss, resident, Executive Director of the Jewish
  Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valleys, Los Angeles County
  Commission on Human Relations Commissioner; Bree; Edgar; Violet Rose Wang,
  resident; Robin S. Toma, Executive Director, on behalf of the Los Angeles County
  Commission on Human Relations and its President llan Davidson; Leticia
  Castaneda, resident; coalition of Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Queer Plus
  (LGBTQ+) elected officials representing the San Gabriel Valley (Jeffrey Prang,
  Assessor, Los Angeles County, President, Los Angeles County LGBTQ+ Elected
  Officials Association; Drew Aleman, Clerk, City of Covina: Florencio Briones, Trustee,
  El Monte Union High School District; Henry Lo, Councilmember, City of Monterey
  Park; Jason Lyon, Councilmember, City of Pasadena; Sasha Renee Perez, Vice
  Mayor, City of Alhambra; Gabriel Quinones, Mayor, City of La Puente; Aaron
  Simental, Board Vice President, Bassett Unified School District; Alton Wang, Board

I  President, Pasadena City College; Thomas Wong, Mayor, City of Monterey Park);
  Gabriel Arellano; Richard Zaldivar; Sophia Pu, resident; Kathay Feng, resident; Rev.
  Tim Hartley, Church of Our Saviour; Edith Gonzalez, representing Los Angeles
  County Supervisor Hilda Solis; Dr. Felix Nunez, resident; Ray C.; Julian Loza, resident;
  David Localio, resident; Jeanne Raya, resident; Erlinda Romo, resident; Florencio
  Briones, President, United Democrats of the San Gabriel Valley; Michelle Brenhaug,
  resident, Vice-Chair HEAR Commission; Florence Simpson, resident; Isaac Chan,
  resident; Lilliana Simpson Castaneda, resident; Jeff Farber, resident; Ariel
  Bustamante; Jorge Herrera Avila, resident; Viki Goto, resident, Chair, HEAR
  Commission; Brad Lemack, resident; Robert Powers; Maria Do, Los Angeles LGBT
  Center; Joey Espinoza-Hernandez; Jackie Calvache; Katie McMahon; Dr. Chasity
  Jennings-Nunez, resident, HEAR Commissioner; and Alan K. Chan.

  The following provided comments or spoke in favor of dissolving the HEAR
  Commission: George Carney, resident; Doug Richter, resident; Sue Fitzsimmons,
  resident; George Valdez, resident; D. Gutierrez, resident; and Cheryl A. Cabot,
  resident.

  The following commented without taking a position: Assemblymember Mike Fong;

I  Congresswoman Judy Chu; and one anonymous commenter.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed at 9:10 P.M. and reconvened at 9:19 P.M. with all Council Members
  present.

  Discussion included the HEAR Commission's purpose to address all human
  relations issues, not a single issue; the Commissioners' changing of narratives and
  character attacks on those who voiced opposing perspectives; Commission
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  Ap ril 16, 2024
   dissolution as a chance to streamline and reassign staff resources; diversity, equity,
  and inclusion will continue; preference for an ad hoc committee instead of a
  commission for best use of City resources; making decisions that are good for the
  entire community; charitable organizations as the best way for advocacy;
  separating the dissolution of the HEAR Commission from support for the LGBTQ
  community; postponing consideration of dissolving the Commission; importance
  of listening to all groups; value of implicit bias training; separation of the All Are
  Welcome program from the dissolution of the HEAR Commission; conflict in the
  viewpoint of oversight responsibility between the Commission and Council; and

I  preference to provide new direction and redefine the responsibilities of the
  Commission.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Harrington, to:

  1. Waive full reading, introduce by title only, and waive future reading of
  Ordinance No. 707 Deleting Title 111, Chapter 33, Sections 33.50-33.57 from the
  San Gabriel Municipal Code to dissolve the HEAR Commission; and waive future
  reading and schedule the second reading and adoption of the Ordinance for
  the next regular City Council meeting.

  2. Appoint, at a later time, two members of the City Council to an ad hoc
  subcommittee and provide specific direction on a human relations issue to
  explore and provide recommendations to the entire City Council.
